items.title: Selectively route keydown events to iframe or parent

raw.title: Selectively route keydown events to iframe or parent
raw.body:
I would like to capure some keydown events (e.g. SPACE) in the parent website and all the other keydown events in an iframe inside the parent.

It seems, as soon as the iframe gets focus (which seems to happen after finishing loading), all keydown events go to the iframe only. Otherwise, all keydown events go to the parent page.

My use case: Chromium-based kiosk system with keyboard, using SPACE (or any other key) to switch between different pages, each showing an iframe with an external app/website, e.g. different games. I have no control over the code of the iframe contents.

In case routing of keydown events is not possible, how can I implement my use case?

items.title: JS changing a DOM element's style transition animation doesn't work

raw.title: JS changing a DOM element's style transition animation doesn't work
raw.body:
I'm trying to understand the principle of FLIP animations.

dom.style.width = '40px';
dom.style.transition = 'width 300ms ease';
dom.offsetHeight;
dom.style.width = '80px';
// This code has an animation effect

dom.style.width = '40px';
dom.style.transition = 'width 300ms ease';
requestAnimationFrame(() => {
  dom.style.width = '80px';
}); 
// This code does NOT have an animation effect. Why?

Below is the specific code. You can change the function executed by setTimeout and then refresh the page. Running run1 will show an animation, while run2 will not.

<!doctype html>
<html>
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <title>document</title>
    <style>
      #dom {
        list-style: none;
        padding: 12px;
        margin: 6px 0;
        background: #e6f0ff;
        border-radius: 6px;
        font-size: 16px;
      }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <div id="dom">dom</div>

    <script>
      const dom = document.getElementById("dom");
      
      const run1 = () => { //Good
        dom.style.width = "40px";
        dom.style.transition = "width 300ms ease";
        dom.offsetHeight;
        dom.style.width = "80px";
      };

      const run2 = () => { //bad
        dom.style.width = "40px";
        dom.style.transition = "width 300ms ease";
        requestAnimationFrame(() => {
          dom.style.width = "80px";
        });
      };

      setTimeout(run2, 3000);
    </script>
  </body>
</html>

items.title: Object does not respond to mouse events

raw.title: Object does not respond to mouse events
raw.body:
I have a JS script that swaps out an element's inner text with an alternative held in a data-* attribute:

<span data-swapinnertext="new text">old text</span>

I have been using this, and it works fine to a point. The point being that there's only one swap on the page:

function swapInnerText0() {
  if (document.querySelectorAll('span[data-swapinnertext]').length > 0) {
    var s, spans = document.querySelectorAll('span[data-swapinnertext]');
    for (s = 0; s < spans.length; s++) {
      var swapText = spans[s].dataset.swapinnertext, innerText = spans[s].innerText;
      spans[s].onmouseover = function() {
        this.innerText = swapText;
      }
      spans[s].onmouseout = function() {
        this.innerText = innerText;
      }
      spans[s].onclick = function() {
        this.innerText = swapText;
        this.onmouseover = null;
        this.onmouseout = null;
        this.removeAttribute('data-swapinnertext');
      }
    }
  }
}

However, if there's more that one, then the onmouseout event replaces the text with the value from the last member of span[s]. I realize why this is the case, so I sought to fix it.

This works, creating temporary data-* cache attributes to hold the text versions for each element:

function swapInnerText1() {
  if (document.querySelectorAll('span[data-swapinnertext]').length > 0) {
    var s, spans = document.querySelectorAll('span[data-swapinnertext]');
    for (s = 0; s < spans.length; s++) {
      spans[s].setAttribute('data-swapcache1', spans[s].dataset.swapinnertext);
      spans[s].setAttribute('data-swapcache2', spans[s].innerText);
      spans[s].onmouseover = function() {
        this.innerText = this.dataset.swapcache1;
      }
      spans[s].onmouseout = function() {
        this.innerText = this.dataset.swapcache2;
      }
      spans[s].onclick = function() {
        this.innerText = this.dataset.swapcache1;
        this.onmouseover = null;
        this.onmouseout = null;
        this.removeAttribute('data-swapinnertext');
        this.removeAttribute('data-swapcache1');
        this.removeAttribute('data-swapcache2');
      }
    }
  }
}

But it is inelegant. What I had tried to earlier do was create a 2D array of the elements and use that to ensure that the text versions for each element were separated from the others:

function swapInnerText2() {
  if (document.querySelectorAll('span[data-swapinnertext]').length > 0) {
    var sp, sw, spans = document.querySelectorAll('span[data-swapinnertext]'), swaps = Array();
    for (sp = 0; sp < spans.length; sp++) {
      var swapText = spans[sp].dataset.swapinnertext, innerText = spans[sp].innerText;
      swaps.push(Array(swapText, innerText));
    } 
    for (sw = 0; sw < swaps.length; sw++) {
      var newText = swaps[sw][0], oldText = swaps[sw][1];
      swaps[sw].onmouseover = function() {
        this.innerText = newText;
      }
      swaps[sw].onmouseout = function() {
        this.innerText = oldText;
      }
      swaps[sw].onclick = function() {
        this.innerText = newText;
        this.onmouseover = null;
        this.onmouseout = null;
        this.removeAttribute('data-swapinnertext');
      }
    }
  }
}

And this is where things go weird. None of the swaps[sw] objects respond to the mouse events. I placed alert() outside the anonymous functions, and they picked up that swaps[sw] were objects, the index and text values for each one, but within the functions nothing happened.

I've racked what little brain I have, and searched extensively, but simply cannot understand why the mouse events don't work in the third version—which I prefer over the second—but do in the other two.

raw.title: Alphabet-only string in typescript (without recursion)
raw.body:
Similar question: Is it possible to annotate alphabet-only string in typescript?

The goal is to create a non-recursive type which will able to detect if the passed string contains only alphabet characters (TS version is 5.9.3)

First attempt (straight):

type Special = Lowercase<string> & Uppercase<string>;

type IsAlphabet<T extends string> = T extends `${string}${Special}${string}` ? never : T;

type Testing = IsAlphabet<"1">; // 1

I thought that the reason is that Special contains empty string so it just checks 3 times empty string and fails because "1" doesn't extends ""

Second attempt (exclude empty string):

type SpecialChar = Lowercase<string> & Uppercase<string>;

type Special = `${SpecialChar}${string}`;

const a: Special = ''; // Type 'string' is not assignable to type '`${SpecialChar}${string}`'
const b: Special = 'a'; // Type 'string' is not assignable to type '`${SpecialChar}${string}`'
const c: Special = '1'; // OK

type IsAlphabet<T extends string> = T extends `${string}${Special}${string}` ? never : T;

type Testing = IsAlphabet<"1">; // 1

I don't know why but Exclude<Lowercase<string> & Uppercase<string>, ''> doesn't exclude the empty string

Third attempt (step by step):

type SpecialChar = Lowercase<string> & Uppercase<string>;

type Special = `${SpecialChar}${string}`;

const a: Special = ''; // Type 'string' is not assignable to type '`${SpecialChar}${string}`'
const b: Special = 'a'; // Type 'string' is not assignable to type '`${SpecialChar}${string}`'
const c: Special = '1'; // OK

type IsAlphabet<T extends string> = T extends Special ? never : (
  T extends`${string}${Special}` ? never : (
    T extends`${Special}${string}` ? never : (
      T extends`${string}${Special}${string}` ? never : T
    )
  )
);

type Testing1 = IsAlphabet<"1">; // never
type Testing2 = IsAlphabet<"1a">; // never
type Testing3 = IsAlphabet<"a1">; // never
type Testing4 = IsAlphabet<"a1a">; // never
type Testing5 = IsAlphabet<"aa1aa">; // "aa1aa"
type Testing6 = IsAlphabet<"HelloWorld">; // "HelloWorld"
  1. Why none of them work? (It seems like string matches only 1 character not the any string)
  2. Is there any way to not use the recursion?

items.title: Direct Upload to S3 from Angular failing with 400 response

raw.title: Direct Upload to S3 from Angular failing with 400 response
raw.body:
I am attempting to upload a file directly to S3 using a put_object presigned URL. When I attempt to upload using a PUT command via the HttpClient I get a 200 on the preflight, but then 400 on the request. No error is thrown that tells me what is incorrect.

I am working in Angular 20+, and Node 20+ for environment references.

File Upload Process

store.ts <snippet>

 async uploadFile(
  dto: FileUploadDto,
  file: File,
  callback?: () => void
) {
  patchState(store, { loading: true });

  try {
    await firstValueFrom(
      fileService.preFlightCommunicationFileUpload(dto).pipe(
        switchMap((response: FileUploadResponseDto) => {
          const {
            presigned_s3_link,
            object_key,
            bucket_name
          } = response;

          return fileService
            .uploadFileToS3(presigned_s3_link, file)
            .pipe(
              switchMap(() => {
                const createDto = {
                  provider_id: dto.provider_id,
                  object_key,
                  bucket_name
                };

                return malpracticeService.saveFile(createDto).pipe(
                  map((response: any) => response)
                );
              })
            );
        })
      )
    );

    callback?.();
  } catch (err) {
    console.error(err);
  } finally {
    patchState(store, { loading: false });
  }
}

file-upload.service.ts

import { Injectable, inject } from '@angular/core';
import { HttpClient, HttpErrorResponse, HttpHeaders } from '@angular/common/http';
import { Observable, throwError } from 'rxjs';
import { catchError } from 'rxjs/operators';
import { environment } from '../../../environment/environment';
import { AuthStore } from '../store/authentication/authentication.store';


export interface FileUploadDto {
  provider_id: number;
  filename: string;
}

export interface FileUploadS3Params {
    object_key: string
    bucket_name: string
}

export interface FileUploadS3PresignedUrl {
    presigned_s3_link: string
}

export interface FileUploadResponseDto extends FileUploadS3Params, FileUploadS3PresignedUrl{ }

@Injectable({
  providedIn: 'root'
})
export class FileUploadService {
  private http = inject(HttpClient);
  private authStore = inject(AuthStore);
  private readonly baseUrl = `${environment.apiBase}`;

  /**
   * Get HTTP headers with authorization token if available
   */
  preFlightCommunicationFileUpload = (dto: FileUploadDto): Observable<FileUploadResponseDto> =>
    this.http.post<FileUploadResponseDto>(`${this.baseUrl}/provider/document`, dto).pipe(
      catchError((error: HttpErrorResponse) => throwError(() => error)))

  uploadFileToS3(url: string, file: File) {
    return this.http.put(url, file, {
      observe: 'response',
      responseType: 'text' as 'json',
      withCredentials: false
    });
  }
}

This is service that the preflight hits to obtain the s3 url. I left the commented out code in there to help give an idea of what we have been working on:

def init_document_upload(self, data: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        # filename = data.get('filename')
        # if not filename:
        #     return {

        #     }

        # elif file_extension.lower() in ['doc']:
        #     content_type = 'application/msword'
        # elif file_extension.lower() in ['docx']:

        #     )
        # elif file_extension.lower() in ['jpg', 'jpeg']:
        #     content_type = 'image/jpeg'
        # elif file_extension.lower() in ['png']:
        #     content_type = 'image/png'

        # bucket_name = data.get("s3_bucket_name") or os.getenv('S3BucketName')

        s3_bucket_name = os.getenv("S3BucketName")
        filename = data.get("filename") or f"{uuid.uuid4()}.bin"
        content_type = data.get("content_type") or "application/octet-stream"

Attempted Fixes

There is a catch to all of this. If we run a simple node function outside of the application:

import { createReadStream } from "node:fs";

items.title: How would you recreate a 3D-like hexagonal progress bar in React Native?

raw.title: How would you recreate a 3D-like hexagonal progress bar in React Native?
raw.body:
Hi everyone 👋

I'm building a mobile app with React Native.

I’m struggling with a front-end component and would really appreciate some guidance.

I need to recreate a hexagonal loading/progress component generated with IA by PNG. It is made of two independent progress bars (two colors) layered in the same shape.

It’s composed of:

  • An outer hexagon
  • An inner hexagon (slightly smaller, with spacing between them)
  • Two independent progress bars (two color sets)
  • A 3D / depth effect using shadows and light (this is where I’m stuck)

items.title: Why is callback reference not observed in useEffect

raw.title: Why is callback reference not observed in useEffect
raw.body:
How do I render a div in a component conditionally based on a component property and the get a reference to that div when it's available?

In this simplified example, the message displayed in the div varies depending on which button is pressed first. I understand why I see div.current is truthy when pressing the second button first. I don't understand why useEffect doesn't observe the change of the div loading upon the change of showHere.

const Message = ({ showHere }) => {
  const divRef = useRef(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (divRef.current) {
      divRef.current.innerHTML = "div.current is truthy";
    }
  }, [divRef, divRef.current]);

  return <>{showHere ? <div ref={divRef}>no message</div> : ""}</>;
};

export default function App() {
  const [showInsideApp, setShowInsideApp] = useState(false);
  const [showInsideComponent, setShowInsideComponent] = useState(false);
  const onButton1Clicked = () => {
    setShowInsideApp(true);
  };
  const onButton2Clicked = () => {
    setShowInsideComponent(true);
  };
  return (
    <div>
      {showInsideApp ? <Message showHere={showInsideComponent} /> : ""}
      <button onClick={onButton1Clicked}>Show in App</button>
      <button onClick={onButton2Clicked}>Show in Component</button>
    </div>
  );
}

The React documentation says:

The useRef Hook returns an object with a single property called current. Initially, myRef.current will be null. When React creates a DOM node for this , React will put a reference to this node into myRef.current. You can then access this DOM node from your event handlers and use the built-in browser APIs defined on it.

I've looked at this answer but it links to outdated documentation, and the current version is pretty different.

Based on this answer and this answer I can monitor on every render by entirely omitting useEffect's second parameter, but I don't want to do that. My real-world problem on which this is based on wanting to configure Coloris's parent element and attach a coloris:pick event to the window but only when the parent element is available.

items.title: input fields become uneditable until Developer Tools is opened

raw.title: input fields become uneditable until Developer Tools is opened
raw.body:
Context:

This is a production Electron desktop application. The issue occurs only on Windows and appears related to focus or hit-testing behaviour rather than application logic.

This is a production Electron desktop application. The issue occurs only on Windows and appears related to focus or hit-testing behavior rather than application logic.

Observed behavior:

Application starts and input fields are editable

Creating a new project still works

Creating the first item causes input fields (descriptions) to become uneditable

Clicking works but the cursor never appears

Typing does nothing and onFocus/onChange never fire

The macOS version works perfectly

Workaround:

Opening View → Toggle Developer Tools once immediately fixes the issue

Closing Developer Tools keeps inputs working

Creating another project breaks inputs again until Developer Tools is toggled

Technology stack:

Electron

React 18

Zustand

react-konva (canvas/PDF viewer overlay)

What we have tried:

Removing stopPropagation and preventDefault from inputs

Removing input onMouseDown handlers

Guarding parent click handlers

Disabling canvas pointer-events while typing

Forcing resize using ResizeObserver and requestAnimationFrame

None of these remove the need to toggle Developer Tools.

Question:
What does opening Developer Tools trigger in Electron or Chromium on Windows that resets focus or hit-testing, and how can this be replicated programmatically or prevented entirely?

This is a business application, so I cannot share the full repository, but I can provide a minimal non-proprietary reproduction if needed.
